title: Where Cryptography Sits in Financial Services
summary: A map of where cryptography protects the financial system, from customer channels and payment messaging to hardware security modules, certificates and digital signatures on contracts and ledgers.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: A map of where cryptography protects the financial system, from customer channels and payment messaging to hardware security modules, certificates and digital signatures on contracts and ledgers.
Learning Objectives: Identify the main uses of cryptography across financial services
Analyse which systems and data carry the highest quantum exposure
Explain why cryptography is often invisible and poorly documented within firms
Syllabus: Secure communications, certificates and public key infrastructure
Payment cards, messaging networks and hardware security modules
Embedded cryptography in legacy and vendor systems
Intended Audience: Supervisors and inspectors responsible for technology, cyber and operational resilience risk
Payments, market infrastructure and digital asset specialists in supervisory and central bank functions
Policy staff and senior managers shaping the authority's cyber and quantum readiness approach
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of cyber, technology risk or operational resilience supervision is helpful. No background in mathematics or cryptography is required.
Core Reading: NIST, FIPS 203, 204 and 205: Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards (2024)
G7 Cyber Expert Group, Public Statement on Planning for the Opportunities and Risks of Quantum Computing (2024)
